questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The cultural aspects of an old university, it being a British university and having a good English programme

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: They sent out multiple emails with the information needed and how to find additional information. Furthermore, they reiterated where and how to find it during in-person lectures etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Multiple emails, multiple oral descriptions during lectures etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorms with or without roommate(s), dorms with or without personal bathrooms, dorms with or without catering - you can mix and match them to fit your need.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You could either be catered or self-catered and if self-catered you could buy meals from the dining halls if you wanted to. The cooking facilites were generally very good, but you generally get better kitchens than the catered students

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Most other students living in the dorms are either freshers or exchange students, so you might end up being friends with a bunch of seventeen-year-olds rather than people your own age.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to pre-register online before you arrived and after arrival you must register via an employee of the uni. Either via zoom or in person when you get there. You should try to do it as quickly as possible, as the spots fill up quickly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You get assigned an academic advisor whom you can always email or set up a meeting with. Furthermore, the university has multiple forms of assistance for free, all you need to do is reach out

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got one of my prioritised classes and because I wanted to sign up in person, one of the classes I wanted was full. However, they have multiple

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it as early as possible - that way you have as much choice as possible

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had honour classes which are quite high academic level as they are what counts for their final grade

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite similar - especially when comparing them to electives in UCPH - mainly seminars, rarely proper lectures (at least in School of English)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Literature and Childhood in the 18th Century
Celtic Modernism

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Celtic Modernism was extremely interesting both regarding the literature, the culture and the analysis

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Most costs were expected - the price of public transport was probably what shocked me the most

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport is quite expensive - around the same or a bit more expensive than Danish public transport.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The very culture is based around societies and athletic clubs, which is where most people find their friends. Thus, in the orientation week, there are fayres to learn about all the different academic, hobby and sport societies. They basically had everything - soccer, polo, theatre, book clubs, individual societies for basically every academic school - whatever you like, there is a society for it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Enroll in societies, go to the pub socials, meet people - but you don't need to go to every single one, you can easily take a day of if you need it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You should definitely go explore the surrounding parts of Fife: Crail, Kingsbarne, the East Fife Coastal Route. If you find time, go to the Highlands. It is absolutely beautiful!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy - the culture is not that difficult from the Danish one.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be curious, be aware that if you take honour classes, you probably don't have as much to do with your classmates, as they already are part of friend groups. However, it is absolutely possible; you just have to make a bit more effort. Be aware that your main friends might become other exchange students and freshers who live in the same dorm as you

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not a lot, really. The biggest problem would probably be understanding Scottish accents.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The focus on academia, the traditions and history of the university, the smallness of the town where you often saw someone you knew in town

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be aware that the written assignments might be more consuming than what you're used to from UCPH
You might have less actual lessons than what you're used to - be aware of learning how to construct your own routine
The scale of grades makes it difficult to translate to the Danish grade system directly

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it - and be aware that the semester flies by far too quickly

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The learning experiences, the friendships made, the experience of living alone in another country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Making a routine that worked when I only had class once a week

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
